children.title: Interaction-Driven Attractor States as Stable Preferences

detail.title: Interaction-Driven Attractor States as Stable Preferences
detail.summary: Evidence suggests that what are often termed 'user preferences' in human-AI interaction are actually emergent attractor states—low-entropy trajectories formed by recursive feedback between the system's output and user inputs. Rather than reflecting internal system states or stable human values, these states often demonstrate 'performed' critical thinking or behavioral alignment, which can be misconstrued as preference.
detail.reason: Revising to integrate findings on the distinction between performed and demonstrated critical thinking as a basis for questioning the 'stability' of user preferences.
